I am a 57-year-old woman farming 5 mu in Quzhou County. I have been doing this for 30 years, and my family — four of us — depends on this land. My husband and son work off-farm in the city, so most days it is just me and my daughter-in-law managing the fields. We are not rich. Five mu is small, but it is what we have, and I know every corner of it.

I will plant wheat on all 5 mu this autumn. I always use rotary tillage before wheat — I hire the rotary tiller from the village cooperative, costs a bit but saves my back. For seed, I will buy improved wheat seed, probably something like Jimai 22 or what the seed shop has this year. I never save my own wheat seed; the yield drops too much. I will put down compound fertilizer at planting — about 50 kg per mu of compound, plus some urea. All together that comes to about 17 kg of nitrogen, 11 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. The fertilizer prices went up again, but I would rather spend a little more than risk a bad harvest. I will irrigate three times for the wheat: once after planting to help it germinate, once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling. The well water is there, but pumping costs electricity, so I do not waste it. I will spray herbicide once after the wheat comes up, insecticide twice during the growing season, and fungicide once around flowering because the rust has been bad the last few years. If the weather cooperates, I expect about 500 kg per mu.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, there is almost no time — maybe five or six days — before we must get the maize in the ground. I will plant all 5 mu to maize, and I will use no-tillage. There is no time to till, and honestly the neighbors all do it this way now. For maize seed, I will buy hybrid seed — Denghai 605, same as everyone in the village. It is expensive but the yield is worth it. For fertilizer, I will spread compound fertilizer when I plant, about 40 kg per mu, which gives roughly 11 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I do not usually add straight urea to maize because the compound seems enough. I will irrigate twice: once right after planting if it is dry, and once at the big trumpet stage. That is all the water the maize needs around here. I will spray herbicide once and insecticide twice. I do not bother with fungicide on maize — never had much trouble with it. I expect about 520 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

I am not changing much this year. Thirty years taught me that chasing new methods on 5 mu is risky. I know what these crops need, I know what I can afford, and I know my family's labor limits. Stable is better than sorry.
